correctness.rationale: The exponential race on vacant edges gives the stated recursion, including R(1,1)=1 and the zero-coefficient boundary terms. Conditional on bridge use, each clique is greedily matched with one fewer vertex, which proves the full vacancy law. Coupling the first attempt as E/beta with a common unit exponential E reduces success to the survival of two independent tags in bridge-deleted cliques. Each survival is E[J(t)] divided by clique size; its derivative is strictly negative at each finite time because the initial state has positive holding probability. This gives strict monotonicity and the weak-rate parity discontinuity. At u=mt the vacancy fraction has drift -x^2+x/m and quadratic-variation rate at most 2/m, giving uniform convergence on compact u-intervals to (1+u)^(-1). The rescaled Laplace law and the early-attempt/late-survival bounds give the three rate regimes. For fixed beta, Jensen's logistic bound dominates the rescaled product by a constant times (1+u)^(-2) up to u=m; above m the O(m^(-2)) product times the exponential kernel has O(m^(-1)) contribution to mP. This justifies the distinct fixed-rate coefficient, including rho=1. Independent exact recursion arithmetic reproduced 1/3, 3/10, 2/7 and 5/26 at unit rate; it did not independently reproduce the full graph or scaling law. The frozen checker was inspected, not run.
